column11: The record of both CM550 first-order filters, the same layout as CM848 ema_filter_state_t (coefficient word* 4, accumulator dword 4). +0 = pointer to the coefficient word (move.w through it): the weight of the previous value in 1/65536, 0 = no filtering (the accumulator is set to the sample). +4 = the Q16.16 filtered value. Field comment must carry both encodings: in the records of 0x34e9a (cm550_signedFirstOrderFilter, signed) it is offset binary, (value + 0x8000) << 16, so 0x80000000 is 0 (every initializer stores 0x80000000, callers preset it with (value << 16) - 0x80000000; 0x80d63a reads 0x9f400000 = 8000); in the records of 0x34f8a (cm550_exponentialMovingAverage, unsigned) it is plain Q16.16 (initializers clr.l). Both filters return the rounded integer part ((accumulator + 0x8000) >> 16). Add as a type-only struct (empty address) ahead of the instances; then set param 1 of 0x34e9a and 0x34f8a to ema_filter_state_t * (see the function rows).

The record of the two CM550 second-order filters 0x34f00 (signed: muls.l / divs.l, saturates to 0x7fffffff / 0x80000000) and 0x34fe0 (unsigned: mulu.l / divu.l, clamps to 0 / 0xffffffff): output = ((c3 - c1 + 0xffff) x output + c1 x (input << 16) - c3 x output_previous) / 0xffff, then output_previous = the old output, output = the new one, return output >> 16. +0 points at c1 (weight of the new input), +4 at c3 (weight of the output before last), +8 output (Q16.16), +C output_previous. Same roles at the same offsets as CM848 second_order_filter_state_t, so the same field names - but CM550 coefficients are in 1/65535 (divide by 0xffff, + 0xffff) where CM848 uses 1/65536 (>> 16, + 0x10000). Type only: NO instance exists in the dumped ROM (refs.py finds no jsr / bsr / pointer to 0x34f00 or 0x34fe0; callers may be in the undumped code above 0x40000).
